answers.stem_only: With allow-list SCPs an action must be allowed at every level from the root down to the account, so an Allow attached at the account cannot add back what the Workloads OU SCP does not allow, and widening the Workloads OU SCP would change every other account. Move the one account into a separate OU (directly under the root, not under Workloads) whose SCP allows the current list plus Athena and AWS Glue; the account keeps its direct FullAWSAccess and the IAM role already allows the actions.

A preventive guardrail is needed, not a detective one, and it must cover console and CLI actions, not only CloudFormation deployments. Write an SCP that denies s3:DeleteBucket (and related delete actions) on the audit log bucket ARNs and attach it once to the Workloads OU, so every member account in the OU inherits it; this binds all IAM users and roles, including account admins.
